prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity macOS desktop app design proposal for Sidefolk, image 1 of a coherent review set.
Primary request: Redesign this real desktop companion app into a calm, mature, exceptionally usable everyday utility. Generate a polished front-on UI mockup, NOT a photograph of hardware, NOT a marketing landing page. One large complete application window occupying most of a 3:2 landscape image with a small outer ivory margin. Crisp readable English text, precise typography, restrained native macOS feel, ample spacing, practical information density.
Product: a personal desktop companion for reminders and dated notes, with optional Claude Code and Codex session monitoring. Personality belongs in one small Pip mascot, not an oversized hero.
Design system MUST follow these exact existing tokens: canvas #F7F3EA, card #FFFCF7, ink #272A33, muted #636773, border #DAD6CD, mint #6FCFB4, mint-soft #DCEFE5. System sans SF Pro; monospace for commands only. Panel titles 28px, body 16px, secondary 14px, metadata 12px at 1x. Spacing 4/8/12/16/24/32; controls radius 10, cards 18, panels 24; comfortably large 44px control targets. Flat opaque surfaces, faint borders, subtle window shadow. No gradients, glassmorphism, heavy texture, bright new colors, massive rounded tiles, excessive nested cards, analytics or token meters.
Composition: A wide macOS app window with traffic lights. Modest full-height left sidebar: tiny charcoal bunny head logo with mint dot and lowercase wordmark "sidefolk". Main navigation "Today" selected in mint-soft, "Reminders", "Notes". After a subtle separator small section label "AI tools" and item "Sessions". Bottom anchored "Actions" then "Settings". Very small Pip at sidebar bottom: charcoal bunny with ivory belly and mint scarf, consistent with our existing identity, no new animal cast.
Top toolbar has a persistent compact input "Tell Pip…" with a speech icon and a labelled "Examples" control; it must read as a quick action input, not chatbot history or search.
Content heading "Today" with smaller "Saturday, 24 October" and a discreet top-right "+ Add reminder" button. Content in two practical columns, wider left and narrower right.
LEFT: an attention section "Needs you" with one subdued bordered card: identity "sidefolk · Codex · Session 04", state badge icon + "Needs you", title "Run project tests?", one sentence "Codex is asking to run a command.", action "Review request". Never put Allow directly on this overview.
Below: heading "Coming up", ONE flat list of three rows, each with simple reminder icon, title, time and a right chevron: "Review launch notes" / "15:00"; "Call Mum" / "18:00"; "Weekly wins" / "Monday, 16:00". Small footer link "All reminders".
RIGHT: section "Work sessions" with compact project rows "sidefolk" / "Codex · Session 04" / Needs you, and "website" / "Claude Code · Session 12" / Working. Icon + written state, status colors only small decorative dots (#FF7A2E Needs you, #FFB547 Working). Small action "Open" beside working session; requesting row has "Review".
Below: "Recent notes", notebook "Weekly wins", excerpt "Shipped the login update.", metadata "Today", small "Add note" action.
Do not repeat a project avatar as a new mascot everywhere. Thin simple outline icons. Every visible control has a sensible label. Clearly legible and coherent, realistic enough to approve a macOS app redesign. Do not add annotations outside the window or invented features.

No computer hardware, no perspective, no hero illustration, no new mascot. The screenshots are the whole deliverable with only a small external label "Light appearance" above left and "Dark appearance" above right.
Each window has macOS traffic lights, a modest category sidebar and a spacious readable main pane. Brand is tiny existing app icon plus "sidefolk". Sidebar title "Settings", labelled input "Search settings" at top.
